lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, eight a.m., her family's flat in Block 208.
**Mum:** The forecast says a **70%** chance of thunderstorms today.
**Dad:** So a **30%** chance of **no** rain. I have a feeling. The picnic is on!
**Kavya:** Dad. Seventy per cent means rain is **likely**.
**Narrator:** Nine a.m. The picnic is off. Kavya's maths teacher, **Mr Tan**, lives one floor up.
**Mr Tan:** Rain plan! I brought my old **game box**. Family Game Night. Well, Game Morning.
**Priya:** Priya. Best friend. I don't **play** games. I **win** them.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about what lives inside Mr Tan's game box.
**Cubert:** Cubert. A **dice**. Six faces, each one **equally likely**. I am perfectly **fair**.
**Mr Tan:** Technically, the singular is **die**.
**Cubert:** Please. Don't call me that. It sounds so... final.
**Ah Boy:** Cubert! Roll me a **seven**!
**Cubert:** I don't **have** a seven. Probability zero. **No. Chance.**
**Narrator:** What Are the Chances? Episode 20: Seventy Per Cent Chance of Game Night.
**Mum:** Game one: **Lucky Dip**. Pick a bag, take a sweet without looking. **Red** wins.
**Mum:** Bag A: **3** red, **5** blue. Bag B: **5** red, **9** blue.
**Ah Boy:** Bag B! It has **more** red ones!
**Dad:** Agreed. I have a feeling about Bag B.
**Cubert:** What matters is the **fraction**. P(event) = **favourable outcomes** ÷ **total outcomes**. **Wanted over All.**
**Kavya:** Bag A: P(red) = 3/8 = **0.375**. Bag B: 5/14, about **0.357**. Bag A wins. Just.
**Cubert:** Every probability lives on a scale from **0**, impossible, to **1**, certain.
**Cubert:** Roll a seven on me: **0**. Roll **under** seven: **1**. An **even** number: 3/6 = **½**. An even chance.
**Priya:** Easy. Bag A: P(red) = **3 : 8**.
**Cubert:** Never a **ratio**. A fraction, a decimal or a percentage: **3/8**, **0.375** or **37.5%**.
**Dad:** I bought a **TOTO** ticket. I either win or I lose. That's fifty-fifty!
**Cubert:** **No. Chance.**
**Kavya:** Winning and losing are **not equally likely**, Dad. Your chance is about **1 in 14 million**.
**Dad:** So there's still a chance.
**Mr Tan:** Game two: the spinner from my childhood. Land on **blue**, win a pineapple tart.
**Spinella:** Spinella, darling. A **spinner**. My sectors are **not** equal. I'm **biased**, and proud.
**Priya:** Three colours, so P(blue) = **⅓**.
**Spinella:** Not equally likely, darling! Red **150°**, blue **90°**, green **120°**. Cut me into **30°** slices.
**Kavya:** **12** equal slices. Blue covers **3**. P(blue) = 3/12 = **¼**. Or from the angle: 90/360.
**Dad:** I was right, though. Seventy per cent rain means thirty per cent **no** rain.
**Kavya:** Rain and no rain are **complements**: P(no rain) = **1 − P(rain)** = 1 − 0.7 = **0.3**. Right maths, Dad. Wrong picnic.
**Spinella:** My cousin, darling: red **0.25**, blue **0.4**, yellow **0.15**. Green is missing!
**Mum:** One colour per spin: **mutually exclusive**, and they cover everything. So they add to **1**.
**Kavya:** And P(red **or** blue) = 0.25 + 0.4 = **0.65**. They can't happen together, so we **add**.
**Mr Tan:** **NOT** means **1 minus**. I'd put it on a T-shirt, but nobody would buy one.
**Narrator:** Twelve noon. Still raining. Lunch is coming up from the hawker centre downstairs.
**Auntie Rose:** Kavya! Rain so heavy, I deliver! Meal deal: **1** of **4** mains, **1** of **3** drinks, **1** of **2** desserts!
**Dad:** 4 + 3 + 2. Nine meal deals. Easy.
**Kavya:** **4** mains × **3** drinks = **12**. Each with **2** desserts: 12 × 2 = **24**.
**Mr Tan:** The **product rule**: **m** ways, then **n** ways, gives **m × n** ways together.
**Auntie Rose:** Twenty-four? Wah. I only cooked six boxes.
**Penny:** Hi! I'm **Penny**! A coin! Heads or tails! Have we met?
**Cubert:** Four times. This morning.
**Penny:** Me plus a dice makes a **sample space**! **2** × **6** = **12** outcomes!
**Ah Boy:** Two coins: two heads, two tails, or one of each. **Three** outcomes, so **⅓** each!
**Kavya:** List **systematically**. Fix the first coin, run through the second: **HH, HT, TH, TT**. **Four** outcomes.
**Penny:** **HT** and **TH** are **different**! Heads then tails, or tails then heads. I wouldn't know. I forget.
**Kavya:** One of each is **2** of the **4**: P = 2/4 = **½**. And two dice? 6 × 6 = **36**.
**Ah Boy:** Can we just eat now?
**Narrator:** Two p.m. Mr Tan's favourite game: the **Two-Dice Horse Race**.
**Mr Tan:** Twelve horses. Roll **two dice**, add the scores, and that horse moves. And never say '**die**' near Cubert.
**Ah Boy:** I pick horse **1**. Number one always wins!
**Dad:** Horse **12**. I have a feeling.
**Priya:** Horse **7**.
**Dad:** Eleven totals, 2 to 12, so every horse has a **1/11** chance. Fair is fair.
**Cubert:** **No. Chance.** The totals are **not** equally likely. The **36 ordered pairs** are. Draw the grid.
**Kavya:** Total **7**: six cells, from 1 and 6 to 6 and 1. P(7) = 6/36 = **⅙**.
**Kavya:** Total **12**: only 6 and 6. P(12) = **1/36**. Sorry, Dad.
**Ah Boy:** So when does my horse, number **one**, move?
**Priya:** Never. Two dice can't make 1. P = **0**. **Impossible.**
**Mum:** House rule: a **six** on either dice gets a bonus move. P(**at least one** six)?
**Kavya:** The six row has **6** cells, the six column **6**, but **(6, 6)** is in both: 6 + 6 − 1 = **11**.
**Cubert:** Or the **complement**: no six on either is 5 × 5 = **25** cells. 1 − 25/36 = **11/36**.
**Narrator:** Four p.m. Horse 7 wins. Horse 1 has not moved.
**Priya:** Puzzle! My class has **30**. **18** play badminton, **15** play chess, **7** do neither.
**Ah Boy:** 18 + 15 + 7 = **40**. Your class has forty people in thirty chairs!
**Venna:** Venna. **Venn diagram**. I seat everyone in exactly **one** region. No exceptions.
**Venna:** Fill me from the **overlap** outwards. 30 − 7 = **23** play at least one.
**Venna:** But 18 + 15 = **33**. The extra **10** were counted **twice**. They play **both**.
**Kavya:** Badminton only: 18 − 10 = **8**. Chess only: 15 − 10 = **5**. Check: 8 + 10 + 5 + 7 = **30**.
**Venna:** P(badminton **or** chess) = (8 + 10 + 5)/30 = **23/30**. The overlap counts **once**. Nobody gets two seats.
**Mr Tan:** Or the formula: P(badminton) + P(chess) − P(both) = 18/30 + 15/30 − 10/30 = **23/30**.
**Mum:** My RC drinks survey: **80** people. Adults: **22** hot, **18** cold. Children: **6** hot, **34** cold.
**Mum:** Pick **anyone**. P(a child with a cold drink)?
**Mum:** Now pick a **child** at random. P(cold drink)?
**Dad:** Same again. **34/80**!
**Kavya:** Only the **40** children count now: 34/40 = **17/20**. Divide by the **group** you're choosing from.
**Mum:** Correct. Dad, you're on hot drinks.
**Narrator:** Five p.m. Ah Boy has found a bottle cap. He will be busy for some time.
**Ah Boy:** It lands **top up** or **top down**. Two ways, so P(top up) = **½**!
**Dr Freq:** Dr Freq. **Relative frequency**. No theory? Then **experiment**. Need. More. Trials.
**Dr Freq:** Relative frequency = **times it happened** ÷ **number of trials**.
**Dad:** Priya has won **every** game today. I think her **lucky dice** is **biased**.
**Dr Freq:** Test it! Roll it **300** times. If it's fair, expect about 1/6 × 300 = **50** of each score.
**Kavya:** 95/300 ≈ **0.32**: nearly **double** 1/6 ≈ **0.17**. A big gap over **300** rolls. **Biased.**
**Priya:** I said it was **lucky**. I never said it was **fair**.
**Mum:** Paper cup, on its side. Kavya: **9** in **20**. Ah Boy: **18** in **50**. Priya: **47** in **130**.
**Dr Freq:** Don't average them. **Pool** them: 74 sides in **200** tosses. 74/200 = **0.37**.
**Narrator:** Eight p.m. Ah Boy has dropped the bottle cap **1000** times.
**Ah Boy:** 100 drops: **0.41**. 1000 drops: **0.384**. It's settling down!
**Dr Freq:** **More trials, better estimate.** P(top up) is about **0.38**. Not ½.

chapters.title: Spin to Win, and Uncle Banyan

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Nine p.m. Ah Boy is planning a stall for next week's school carnival.
**Ah Boy:** **Spin to Win**! **$1** a go. **5** equal sectors. Land on gold, win **$3**!
**Cubert:** **Expected number = probability × number of trials.** P times the tries.
**Kavya:** **200** players, P(win) = **1/5**. Expect 1/5 × 200 = **40** winners.
**Mr Tan:** **About** $80. Expected is a **prediction**, not a **promise**.
**Mum:** Backwards: we expect **80** reds in **200** picks. P(red)?
**Mum:** Forecast: **70%** chance of rain on Sunday, and on Monday.
**Dad:** Penny's landed **heads** five times in a row. **Tails** is due. I have a feeling.
**Penny:** Hi! I'm Penny! Have we met?
**Cubert:** A coin has **no memory**. P(tails) is still **½**. Each flip is **independent**.
**Uncle Banyan:** Uncle Banyan. **Tree diagram**. Sunday: rain **0.7**, dry **0.3**. Each set of branches adds to **1**.
**Kavya:** Rain **and then** rain: **multiply** along the path. 0.7 × 0.7 = **0.49**.
**Priya:** Exactly **one** wet day: **0.21** + **0.21**. **Add** the paths: **0.42**.
**Uncle Banyan:** All four ends: 0.49 + 0.21 + 0.21 + 0.09 = **1**. **AND, multiply. OR, add.**
**Mr Tan:** **3** strawberry, **2** lemon. Eat one, then another: **without replacement**. The bag **changes**.
**Kavya:** P(both strawberry) = 3/5 × 2/4 = **3/10**.
**Ah Boy:** Or I eat all five, and the probability is **one**.

chapters.title: Game Night saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, Game Night would like to save you some marks.
**Priya:** One. A probability is a **fraction**, **decimal** or **percentage**. **3/10**, not **3 : 10**.
**Dad:** Two. A probability **bigger than 1**? Something's wrong. Even my feelings stay under one.
**Penny:** Three. **HT** and **TH** are **different**. List them both. I'd write that down, but I'd forget.
**Mum:** Four. '**A child** is chosen'? Divide by the **children**, not the grand total.
**Venna:** Five. 'This **or** that'? Count the **overlap** once. Nobody gets two seats.
**Dr Freq:** Six. Combining experiments? **Pool** the totals. Never **average** the relative frequencies.
**Narrator:** What Are the Chances? will return.
**Narrator:** Sunday, six a.m. The rain has finally stopped.
**Mum:** Ah Boy? Have you been rolling dice **all night**?
**Ah Boy:** Horse one still hasn't moved. But I have a feeling.
**Dad:** Me too, son. Me too.
**Cubert:** Total of one. Probability... zero.
